_comment: Blurb and filter tags per repo name in github-repos.json. Tags: net, sql, sec, api, fe, ai, py, cld. Add "hide": true to leave a repo off the board.

AdminHelpDesk.blurb: An admin's toolbelt for Valheim server hosts. Whatever the vanilla console doesn't give you, this fills in.

ai-agent-mcps.blurb: Ten MCP services in one monorepo, consolidated from separate repos with full history: workbenches for C, .NET, pygame, chess engines, DOS reverse engineering, databases, SSIS, Steam and Valheim modding, plus RAG-backed knowledge services on ChromaDB. All speak the stateless MCP 2026-07-28 protocol.

AutoHeim.blurb: A BepInEx plugin and launcher that lets Claude Code drive the Valheim client with no human at the keyboard: create characters and worlds, host or join, move, fight, build, and read what's on screen.

Battlestar.blurb: A client/server multiplayer space shooter in Python, with its own socket layer and a typed message protocol between server and fighters.

bchess.blurb: A bitboard chess engine in C with UCI support, move ordering and profile-guided builds. Started in 2016 and still being tuned.

betl-dotnet.blurb: A pure .NET 9 implementation of Better ETL, aiming for full pipeline-file compatibility with betl-native. Runs natively on Windows and ships as a .NET global tool, with 150+ conformance tests.

betl-native.blurb: Better ETL: an open-source SSIS replacement. Pipelines are plain YAML you can diff and review, the engine is C with Apache Arrow types, providers load through a stable C ABI, and Lua handles expressions and tasks.

betl-tools.blurb: Tooling for the betl ecosystem: an SSIS .dtsx to YAML converter, a browser-based pipeline viewer/editor with a live demo on GitHub Pages, and container packaging.

Bretaheim.blurb: Ultima V: Warriors of Destiny rebuilt inside Valheim as a BepInEx/Jötunn mod. Reads the player's own copy of Ultima V at runtime; no game data is distributed.

claude-sandbox-core.blurb: A data-driven scaffold for running Claude Code in a sandboxed container against per-domain MCP service stacks. One image for every domain; a config file picks the services, mounts and environment.

DarkAgesAI.blurb: A browser game driven by large language models: FastAPI services behind nginx, a React front end, and Hugging Face or OpenAI models doing the storytelling.

DayNightRobust.blurb: A Valheim day/night mod rebuilt so it stops breaking every time the game ships a point release.

dayz-map-chat.blurb: Talk to your DayZ map: a single-page map intel tool that answers questions about Chernarus through the Claude API.

DayZ3dMap.blurb: A 3D wireframe map of Chernarus and Livonia in the browser, extracted from your own DayZ install: terrain contours, every building, 2.5 million trees and the road network. Fly into a town and its buildings become holograms, interiors and all.

DayZMissions.blurb: Scripted missions for DayZ dedicated servers on Linux, with deploy, client-launch and headless smoke-test tooling.

DiscordLogSync.blurb: Push selected Valheim server events to Discord. Good for admins who want to know when their server is on fire without staring at it.

DjangoMQDemo.blurb: A small Django platform slice: REST APIs, background jobs and a third-party integration on Django, DRF, Celery, PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ, all running in rootless podman containers.

DualBoot.blurb: Notes and cheat sheets for keeping a Windows/Linux dual boot alive, including rescuing a broken GRUB.

EepeyDeepey.blurb: Companion piece to NightTerrors. Where that one punishes sleeping, this one rewards it.

InventoryQuest.blurb: A server-authoritative multiplayer climb-the-mountain game where the real game is inventory management. Java 21 and Spring Boot, with htmx over WebSockets; the browser holds no game state.

Lockscreen.blurb: A replacement Android lock screen built with React Native and Expo.

MPServerTOD.blurb: A system-tray app that tracks the in-game time of day on DayZ and SCUM servers, so you join when it's daylight.

NetworkRelay.blurb: A certificate-authenticated SOCKS5 relay for secure tunnelling: mutual TLS client certificates plus IP-bound, time-limited tokens, with no changes needed to the applications using it.

NightTerrors.blurb: Sleep used to be safe in Valheim. Now it's a gamble: most nights pass uneventfully; some don't.

SCUM-Mods.blurb: Server-side mods and reverse-engineering notes for SCUM dedicated servers, running inside the server via UE4SS so players need nothing installed and BattlEye stays on.

ServerBrowser.blurb: A real-time DayZ-style server browser: WebSocket updates, filtering, a live stats dashboard and SQLite storage behind nginx. Concept to working prototype in about two hours.

SetupLinuxDev.blurb: Scripts that turn a fresh Linux install into a development machine, including a gamescope build.

spacewar.blurb: Spacewar! reborn: two ships, a star and gravity. The seed of all video games, redone in Python.

SpaceWar2.blurb: The sequel, now networked: a WebSocket server runs the physics at 60Hz and up to four Pyglet clients render it, with GLSL effects.

StableDiffClientMinimal.blurb: A minimal, GPU-aware Stable Diffusion client with explicit VRAM control and pinned CUDA/PyTorch, distilled to what's needed for reproducible image generation.

stupidcodetricks.blurb: A shed in the backyard for storing dumb things with no practical use whatsoever.

TranslinkRealtimeApp.blurb: A live 'next service in X minutes' departures board with a live map, covering public transport across Queensland, Victoria, NSW, South Australia, Western Australia and the Northern Territory.

trebuchet.blurb: An immutable-first language that compiles to readable C# and C++20: inferred effects, errors as values, type classes, lazy sequences and property tests, with services that plug into ASP.NET dependency injection. Its flagship application is valslöngva, a Valheim mod manager whose domain logic is pure Trebuchet, hosted in a thin C# wrapper: a static class behind the externs and the ASP.NET process that serves the browser UI.

TuckMyChooksIn.blurb: Build beds for your Valheim chickens, so your chooks aren't running around clucking while you're trying to skip the night.

Ultima5Revolutions.blurb: Ultima V (DOS, 1988) decompiled to Rust: every function of the original executable and its 23 overlays translated, reading all data from your own copy of the game.

UltimatePyve.blurb: A drop-in replacement engine for Ultima V: the original game data running through a modern Python engine built for modding, debugging and expansion.

UnifiedControlPanel.blurb: One desktop control panel for the Windows settings scattered across a dozen dialogs: accounts, devices, network, security, services, storage and more.

ValheimKillFeed.blurb: A Quake-style kill feed for Valheim, so the chaos finally has receipts.

ValheimScheduledMessages.blurb: Broadcast messages to a Valheim server on a schedule: rules, restart warnings, lore drops.
